 Vth Addl. S.C.Judge & XXIVth ACJM  SCCH-20, Mayohall Unit, Bangalore  JUDGMENT Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the daughter of Late Dhattatraya.

That on 10.08.2023 at about at about 11.55 PM., Dattatraya S/o Late Gundu Rao was traveling as passenger in a car bearing No.KA-05-F9366 on Bangalore - Mysore Road, Channapatna Taluk, wherein the driver of Eicher Goods Carrier bearing No.KA-07-A-4562 drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the car, due to which, Dattatreya fell down and sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Later he was shifted to Chamundeshwari Hospital at Chennapatna,
wherein he died due to the accidental injuries.
Autopsy was conducted.
Petitioners have performed the funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that deceased Dattatreya was aged about 69 yeas of age, as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was doing Real estate business and was earning Rs.50,000/- p.a, and he was the only earning member for their family.

They alleged accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.150/2023.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.1 is the of the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurer, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.

4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they appeared through their counsel,
filed vakalath and their respective written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.

5. Respondent No.1 contended that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the car and he was having no valid DL as on the date of the accident Respondent No.2 contended that insured has violated the policy conditions and the driver of the lorry was not having valid DL as on Pushpa vs Roshan Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195565770/
2 the date of the accident and they prays this Tribunal to dismiss the petition.
6. In order to prove the case, Petitioner No.2 examined herself as PW-1 and she produced and marked 12 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 12 and she is fully cross examined.

Respondent No.2 examined its official as RW-1 and RTO official as RW-2, produced and marked 9 documents which are Ex.D1 and D9 and they are fully cross examined.
7.
I have heard the arguments form the counsel appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

1. Chandrakala and another Vs Dilip Kumar and another - MFA No.1662/2023 (MV-D) The High court of Karnataka - order dated 02.07.2024.

sentences.text: On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 10.08.2023 at about 11.55 PM., deceased Dattatraya S/o Late Gundu Rao was proceeding in a car bearing No.KA-05-F9366 on Bangalore - Mysore Road, Channapatna Taluk, wherein driver of Eicher Goods Carrier bearing No.KA-07-A-4562 drove it in a rash and negligent manner and without observing the traffic rules dashed against the deceased car, due to which,
deceased
fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the way to the Hospital?

2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
Addl Issues:
1.Whether respondents proves that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the car bearing Reg No.KA-05-AF-9366 and further proves that the driver of the said vehicle drove the same without having valid driving license as on the date of accident?

Pushpa vs Roshan Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195565770/
3
2. Whether respondent No.1 proves that her vehicle has been falsely implicated in the case as contended in the written statement ?

9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative  Issue no.2: In partly Affirmative,
 Addl Issue no.1: In the Negative  Addl Issue no.2: In the Negative  Issue No.3: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issues No.1 & 2 and Addl Issue No.1 & 2 :-
I have taken these issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.2 and the daughter of the petitioner No.1 and late Dattatraya, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.
11.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, which belongs to respondent No.1.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR, complaint,
mahazar, sketch, IMV report, inquest, PM report, final report which are at Ex.P1 to 8.
12.
On perusal and analysis of the aforesaid documents, it is evident that Late Dattatreya has died due to the accidental injuries.
Ex.P.6 & 7 are the inquest and PM report, the recitals reveals that the Dattatreya had died due to the head injury in the accident.
Ex.P8 is the final report filed after fair investigation and it is not disputed by the respondents.
It is true that one Siddaraju s/o Gavi Siddaiah was the driver of the offending vehicle and the driver of the car is not charge sheeted for any offence.
The final report is the prime facie proof for the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Respondent no.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle has not chosen to contest the petition.
Respondents have not chosen to examine the IO of the case and the driver of the car to probabilise their contention as contended in the written statement.

In the cross examination of RW-1, he admitted the final report filed by the IO as per Ex.P.8 is correct, ExD2, 3, 9 are the copies of the insurance policy of offending vehicle, driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle and RC of the offending vehicle.
The entry therein establishes that the said documents are valid as on the date of the accident.
Further in the cross examination of RW-2, he deposed that Siddaraju was having valid driving license as per Ex.D8 to drive the LMV vehicle.
Apparently there is fundamental violation of the policy conditions by the insured.
13. Admittedly the accident occurred on 10.08.2023, petitioners have not tendered the evidence to Pushpa vs Roshan Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195565770/

4 substantiate the nature of work and the income of the deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.16,000/- P.M has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2023.
14. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.12, the year of birth of the deceased is 1953.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 70 years.
Accordingly the multiplier 5 is applicable.
15. Deceased was 70 years as on the date of the accident, hence future prospectus cannot be considered .
Deceased has left behind 3 dependents accordingly 1/3 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

16. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs.16,000/-
2 Less; 1/3for personal expenses Rs.5,333/- 4 Monthly income Rs.10,667/-
Rs.10,667 (income)X 12 (month) X 5 Rs.6,40,020/- (Multiplier ) Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.6,40,020/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.
17. Loss of estate;

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.
18 .

Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.

19. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.
In the present case petitioner no.1 to 3 are the wife and daughter of the deceased and they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.1,20,000/- as compensation under this head.

Except the aforesaid compensation amount,
petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

20. In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl Compensation under the Head Amount No. 1 Loss of dependency Rs.6,40,020/-
2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-

5
3 Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-

TOTAL Rs.7,90,020/-
[S
In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.7,90,020/-.
21. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
22. Liability:
The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle.
Ex.D9 is B Extract of the offending vehicle and it is a goods carrier having unladen weight of 3440 kgs.
Admittedly as on the date of the incident no goods/ laguage were present in the offending vehicle and it was empty.
Respondents have not taken any specific contention in their written statement regarding the details, terms and condition of the registration certificate and permit of the offending vehicle.
Ex.D3, 8 are the copies of the license of the driver of the offending Lorry and it was valid as on the date of the incident.
Admittedly the gross weight of the offending vehicle does not exceeds 7500 kgs and it falls under the category of LMV.

Further there is no requirement to obtained separate endorsement on the license to drive the transport vehicle and if a driver is holding license to drive LMV, he can drive the transport vehicle also without any endorsement to that effect.
In the present case driver of the offending vehicle is having valid license to drive LMV and offending vehicle was empty and its unladen weight was 3440 kgs.
as per Ex.D9.
Such being the case, the unladen weight of the offending vehicle has to be considered to verify and decide the nature and type of the license of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is also true that it is not the specific defence of the respondent No.2 that the holder of LMV license cannot drive the unladen vehicle.

Accordingly considering the license which are at Ex.D3 & 8, tribunal can safely hold and infer that the driver of the offending vehicle is competent to drive the offending vehicle (unladen weight 3440 Kgs).
Further more, the insured has not violated the policy conditions and insurer has failed to probabilise their contention as contended in the written statement.
Inasmuch, the version of the petitioners based on the evidence cannot be ignored.

In the authority relied on by counsel appearing for the Respondent No.2, wherein the concept of excluding the interest on the future prospectus, the concept of pay and recovery and classification and category of vehicle, driving license are categorically discussed.
In the present case facts and attending circumstances and nature and classification of offending vehicle is entirely different.

In Bajaj Allianz Insurance company Vs Ramba Devi Pushpa vs Roshan Shariff on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195565770/
6 - Supreme court of India, order dated 08.03.2022, and 06.11.2024 wherein the Hon'ble Apex court has categorically held regarding the classification of vehicles and driving license details.

sentences.text: With great respect to the aforesaid authority and with great respect to the authority relied on by counsel appearing for R2 and with the aforesaid discussion, this Tribunal has come to the firm conclusion based on the evidence placed on record, that insurance company that is respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation with interest.
Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, Issue No.2 in partly affirmative and Addl issue No.1 & 2 in the negative.
23. Issue No.3;
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.7,90,020/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.

Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 70% petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled for 15% each in the total compensation amount with interest.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioners are permitted to withdraw their entire share of compensation amount with interest there on by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020, Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.7,90,020/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.

Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 70% petitioner No.2 and 3 are entitled for 15% each in the total compensation amount with interest.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioners are permitted to withdraw their entire share of compensation amount with interest there on by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020, Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
